texts.li: An imperial steward at {PLACE} has written to every settlement within a month's ride. The Empire is raising a levy for a campaign on the far side of the world, and it expects its neighbors to contribute, in silver or in kind.\n\nIt isn't a tax, the letter says. It is an opportunity to be remembered.

[titled] An imperial steward at {PLACE} has written to the colony, addressing its titled colonists by their full honors. The Empire is raising a levy for a campaign far away, and those who hold its titles are expected to set an example.\n\nThe letter is polite. It is also very clear.

summaries.li: {FACTION} will ask the colony for a share of the levy. Paying earns their goodwill; refusing costs some, though nobody marches over it.
[paid] The colony has paid its share of the levy. {FACTION} will remember it.

texts.li: The steward's clerk has arrived with the assessment: {COUNT} silver, to be delivered to {PLACE} within the week. The clerk is young, sunburnt, and very sorry about the whole thing.\n\nHe mentions, without being asked, that settlements which pay in full are listed by name in the campaign's dispatches.
[titled] The steward's clerk has arrived with the assessment: {COUNT} silver. For a colony with titled members, the clerk notes, the Empire would expect nothing less, and would notice anything less.

li.label: Pay in full ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The clerk counts the silver twice, writes the colony's name in his ledger with a flourish, and rides back to {PLACE}.
li.deed: paid its share of the Empire's levy

li.label: Pay half, with apologies
li.outcome: The clerk accepts half, writes something careful in his ledger, and assures the colony that the steward is an understanding man.
li.deed: paid part of the Empire's levy

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The clerk is told the colony can't spare the silver. He writes that down too, and rides off without finishing his tea.

texts.li: A rider from {PLACE} brought a copy of the campaign's dispatches. The colony is named among the settlements that paid the levy in full, between a mining town and a monastery.
The Empire's campaign has its silver and has gone wherever campaigns go. {FACTION} at {PLACE} speak well of the colony, and the steward has sent a short, formal letter of thanks.

li.chronicle: The colony paid its share of the Empire's levy.

titles.li: The levy is raised without us

texts.li: The Empire's campaign has its silver, from other settlements. The steward at {PLACE} has not written again, which is its own kind of letter.

li.chronicle: The colony refused the Empire's levy.

texts.li: The Empire's campaign has its silver and has moved on. Life around {PLACE} goes back to what it was.

li.chronicle: The Empire raised a levy around {PLACE}.

texts.li: A unit of the Empire's troops walked away from their posts near {PLACE} last week, and some of them took their gear with them. The Empire has posted a reward for every one brought back.\n\nImperial patrols are on the roads, asking questions at every gate. Some of the deserters are hiding in the hills. Some of them are only tired.

[titled] The Empire has written to the colony's titled colonists in person: deserters from a garrison near {PLACE} are loose in the region, and those who hold the Empire's honors are expected to help bring them in.\n\nSome of the deserters joined the ones who fight the Empire outright. Most are only tired of it.

summaries.li: A deserter may come to the colony asking for help. {FACTION} will pay for any that are handed over, and won't thank anyone who hides one.
[sheltered] The colony took in a deserter. {FACTION}'s patrols are still asking questions.

texts.li: A young soldier in a torn imperial uniform came out of the trees at dusk with empty hands raised. The soldier deserted from the garrison near {PLACE} and hasn't eaten in three days.\n\nThe deserter doesn't want to fight anyone, only to stop running. The patrols are a day behind.

[winter] {A_nameDef} found a deserter from {FACTION}'s garrison half-frozen in the woodshed this morning, still in uniform. The soldier says the officer ordered a village burned, and that was the end of it. That was a week ago.\n\nAn imperial patrol passed the colony yesterday, asking after exactly this.

li.label: Let the deserter stay
li.outcome: The deserter was given a bed and a change of clothes, and the uniform went into the fire. {FACTION} will hear of it sooner or later.

li.label: Hand the deserter over for the reward
li.outcome: The deserter didn't fight when the patrol came. The officer paid the reward in full and thanked the colony for its loyalty.

li.label: Feed the deserter and send them on
li.outcome: The deserter ate two bowls of stew, took a loaf for the road, and was gone before the patrol came by. Nobody at the colony had seen anyone.

texts.li: An imperial patrol stopped at the gate and asked {A_nameDef} whether anyone in uniform had come through. {A_nameDef} said no, and offered them water. They took the water.
The Empire's patrols have moved on from the roads around {PLACE}. Some of the deserters were caught, some got away, and the reward posters are peeling off the walls.
[sheltered] The Empire's patrols have moved on. One of the deserters they were looking for is mending fences at the colony and answering to a new name.
[handedover] The Empire's patrols have moved on. At {PLACE} they say the deserters who were caught were sent to the far end of the world, where the fighting is.

li.chronicle: The Empire hunted deserters on the roads around {PLACE}.

texts.li: {FACTION} is choosing its consuls for the coming year. The senate at {PLACE} is split between the old families, who want things as they are, and the reformers, who want land for the veterans and bread for the city.\n\nCanvassers from both sides are out on every road, shaking every hand they can reach. Some of them have reached the colony.

summaries.li: Both sides would like the colony's backing, which mostly means its silver. Whoever wins will remember who helped.
[reform] The colony has backed the reformers in {FACTION}'s election.
[oldfamilies] The colony has backed the old families in {FACTION}'s election.

texts.li: Two canvassers from {PLACE} arrived within an hour of each other and are pretending not to see one another. The man from the old families talks about order, the reformer about bread. Either would carry the colony's good wishes back to the senate, along with {COUNT} silver for the campaign.\n\n{A_nameDef} has listened to both, and has opinions.

li.label: Back the reformers ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The reformer pockets the silver, shakes every hand in the colony, and promises that {FACTION} won't forget its friends.

li.label: Back the old families ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The canvasser for the old families accepts the silver as if it were owed, and leaves a letter of thanks with a heavy seal.

li.label: the silver for the old families

li.deed: backed the old families in {FACTION}'s election

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: Both canvassers are given a meal and nothing else. They leave together, still not speaking.

texts.li: Word from {PLACE}: the candidates are paying for games in the city, with chariot races, a play and free bread. {A_nameDef} has been describing the chariots to anyone who stands still long enough.
[reform] The reformers have carried the vote, and the new consuls have already started on their promises. A letter from {PLACE} thanks the colony by name for its early support.
[oldfamilies] The old families have held the consulship, and things at {PLACE} will go on as they were. A letter with a heavy seal thanks the colony for knowing its friends.
[reform] The old families have kept the consulship. The new consuls know exactly which settlements paid for the reformers' campaign, and their first letters to the colony are cool.
[oldfamilies] The reformers have taken the consulship. They know who paid for the old families' campaign, and say they hold no grudges, in a way that suggests they hold several.
{FACTION} has its new consuls. The canvassers have gone home, the posters are coming down, and the colony was never once mentioned in the speeches.

Somebody from {PLACE} found gold in a creek bed last month, and now every settler with a pan and a mule is heading for the hills. {FACTION}'s mayor has given up trying to keep the town's blacksmith at his forge.\n\nProspectors are on every road. Most of them will find nothing. All of them will need beans, rope and somewhere to sleep.

summaries.li: Travelers and traders come by more often. Prospectors may ask to try their luck on the colony's land.

texts.li: A prospector from {PLACE} with a bent pan and a very patient mule wants to work the stream below the colony for a week. He offers the colony a third of anything he finds, and swears on his mother that there's color in that water.\n\n{A_nameDef} has looked at the stream every day for a year and never seen any.

li.label: Let him dig, for a third
li.outcome: The prospector worked the stream for a week, singing. At the end of it he left the colony its third, weighed out on a little brass scale: more than anyone expected.
li.riskOutcome: The prospector worked the stream for a week and found mud, a boot and some very surprised frogs. He left in good spirits, heading for the next creek.

li.label: Send him on
li.outcome: The prospector tipped his hat, said the colony would be sorry, and led his mule off up the valley.

texts.li: Another string of prospectors passed the colony this morning, headed for the hills above {PLACE}. {A_nameDef} sold one of them a coil of rope for twice what it was worth and has been insufferable since.
The creek near {PLACE} has given up what little gold it had. The prospectors are drifting home or on to the next rumor, and {FACTION}'s blacksmith is back at his forge.

li.chronicle: The gold fever near {PLACE} played out.
